t.1.43.1: Then that king, having gone to the ocean followed by Gaṅgā, entered the underworld beneath the earth, where they had been reduced to ashes.
t.1.43.2: Then, O Rāma, when the ashes had been flooded by the waters of Gaṅgā, Brahmā, the lord of all the worlds, spoke these words to the king.
t.1.43.3: O tiger among men, the sixty thousand sons of the great-souled Sagara have been delivered, and like gods they have gone to heaven.
t.1.43.4: As long as the water of the ocean remains in the world, O king, so long will the sons of Sagara dwell in heaven like gods.
t.1.43.5: And this Gaṅgā shall be your eldest daughter, and by the name given by you she shall indeed abide renowned in the world.
t.1.43.7: O lord of men, here you must offer the water libations for all your forefathers; O king, fulfill your vow.
t.1.43.6: The divine Gaṅgā is called Tripathagā and also Bhāgīrathī; because she sanctifies the three paths, she is therefore remembered as Tripathagā.
t.1.43.8: For, O king, this cherished wish was not attained then by that forefather of yours, exceedingly glorious and foremost among the righteous.
t.1.43.9: Likewise, dear one, Aṃśumant, of unequalled splendour in the world, though he longed to bring Gaṅgā down, could not fulfil his vow.
t.1.43.10: By the royal sage, virtuous, whose splendor equals that of the great sages, whose austerity is equal to my own, and who stands firm in the dharma of a kṣatriya.
t.1.43.11: O greatly fortunate one, O sinless one, even your exceedingly splendid father Dilīpa, though he prayed for it, was not able to bring Gaṅgā down.
t.1.43.12: That vow has been fully accomplished by you, O bull among men; you have won in the world supreme glory, most highly esteemed.
t.1.43.13: And since the descent of Gaṅgā has been accomplished by you, O tamer of foes, by this deed you have attained the great abode of dharma.
t.1.43.14: O best of men, immerse yourself in these waters, ever fit for bathing; O tiger among men, become pure and obtain the fruit of merit.
t.1.43.15: Perform the water-offering for all your forefathers. May good fortune be yours; I shall go to my own world. Now depart, O king.
t.1.43.16: Having spoken thus, the lord of the gods, the grandsire of all the worlds, of great renown, went back to the world of the gods just as he had come.
t.1.43.17: Bhagīratha too, the illustrious royal sage, offered the finest water-libation to the sons of Sagara in due order and according to rule; then, having completed the water-rites and been made pure, the king entered his own city.
t.1.43.18: His purpose fulfilled, O best of men, he ruled his own kingdom. And the people rejoiced on gaining him as their king, O Rāghava; their grief was gone, their aims were fulfilled, and they were free from distress.
t.1.43.19: This, O Rāma, is the full account of the Gaṅgā that I have related to you. May you attain well-being, good fortune be with you; the time of the evening twilight is passing.
t.1.43.20: This tale of the Descent of Gaṅgā has been narrated by me; it bestows wealth, fame, long life, heaven, and also sons.
